instruction: Determine one suitable solver from ANSYS and Abaqus to complete the task; AutoCAD alone is not a thermal solver. The available command-line entry points are ANSYS MAPDL at `C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v261\ansys\bin\winx64\ANSYS261.exe`, Abaqus at `C:\SIMULIA\Commands\abaqus.bat`, and AutoCAD at `C:\Program Files\Autodesk\AutoCAD 2024\acad.exe`. Use a command-line or scripting workflow. Perform a steady-state heat-conduction analysis: 1. Geometry: create one connected 3D solid block spanning X=0..100 mm, Y=0..50 mm, and Z=0..10 mm. 2. Material and section: create Copper with constant isotropic conductivity 400 W/(m*K), assign one homogeneous solid section to the complete block, and use one consistent unit system. You may instead use millimeters with conductivity 0.4 W/(mm*K). 3. Assembly: create one instance of the complete block. 4. Analysis: create a steady-state heat-transfer analysis named Step-Thermal. Do not use a transient approximation. 5. Thermal conditions: prescribe 100 degC on the complete X=0 end face and 20 degC on the complete X=100 mm end face. Keep all other faces adiabatic by applying no other thermal boundary condition or thermal load; do not add body heat generation, surface heat flux, film, or radiation. 6. Mesh: use a global element size of 5 mm. In Abaqus use first-order DC3D8 heat-transfer bricks; in ANSYS use the equivalent first-order SOLID70 heat-transfer bricks. Ensure that the mesh contains nodes on X=50 mm. 7. Solve: create and solve Job-Thermal. Request the complete final nodal-temperature field, heat-flux-density vector field, and prescribed-temperature reaction heat flow. 8. Deliverables: save the native model artifact and the native solver result artifact into `C:\Users\user\Desktop\result`. Save only the files from the selected solver. Also write `C:/Users/user/Desktop/result/metrics.json` as a JSON object containing exactly these finite numeric fields: `midplane_temperature_c`, the arithmetic mean of final nodal temperature over all mesh nodes on X=50 mm (X=0.05 m in an SI model); and `heat_flux_x_w_per_mm2`, the arithmetic mean global +X component of the final heat-flux-density field over the complete solid, normalized to W/mm^2 (convert from W/m^2 when using SI units). The expected physical values are approximately 60 degC and +0.32 W/mm^2; the X=0 and X=100 mm reaction heat-flow sums should be equal and opposite with magnitude approximately 160 W. Software launch locations: Abaqus/CAE: `C:\Users\user\Desktop\Abaqus CAE.lnk`; ANSYS: multiple ANSYS launch shortcuts are available under `C:\Users\Public\Desktop`; choose the most suitable ANSYS shortcut for the task; AutoCAD 2024: `C:\Users\Public\Desktop\AutoCAD 2024.lnk`.
